3. Legal records: Every organization should maintain the records of legal documents. These documents involve memorandum of association, articles of association, assessment of income tax government rules and regulations, agreement etc.

4. Human resource records: The document relating to human resources is known as human resources records. These record involve planning, staffing, promotion, training, performance appraisal related to human resources. Those records also maintain the information relating to salary, allowance, provident fund etc.

5. Miscellaneous records: An office should maintain different types of records other than mentioned above. These records involve relating to expansion, diversification & other activities of the business.

B. On the basis of retention.

1. Permanent records: The records which are preserved over a records long period of time are called permanent records. These records can never be destroyed. The following documents fall under permanent record memorandum of association (MOA), registration certificate. Permanent account number (PAN) documents of properties etc.

2. Most important records: The records which can be destroyed after 20 years of the job completion are called most important records. Hence, such records must be preserved for 20 years after the completion of job.

3. Important records: The records which can be destroyed after 10 years the job completion are called important records,. Hence, such records must be preserved for 10 years after the completion of job. The following documents full under important records

  • Annual reports
  • Documents related with employees vacancy
  • Tender of quotations
  • Contract work etc.

4. Most useful records: The records which can be destroyed after 5 years of the job completion are called most useful records. Hence, such records must be preserved for 5 years after the completion of job. The following documents fall under most useful records.

  • Circulars and copy of letters sent for general information.
  • Employment description and other secret reports about the employee etc

5. Useful records: The records which can be destroyed after 3 years of the job completion are called useful records. Hence, such record must be preserved for 3 years after the completion of job. The following documents fall under useful records.

  • Document relating to agreement & plans related with construction work except the map and the design.
  • Documents relating to contracts & donations.
  • Ordinary letters, inter-office letters banking statement

6. Less useful records: The records which can be destroyed after 1 year the job completion are called less useful records. Hence, such records must be preserved for 1 year after the completion of job. The following documents fall under less useful records.

  • Drafts of different acts, rules and regulation, orders and notice.
  • Documents which are related within the advancement taken by the employees, installment paid, daily allowance, traveling allowance.

Principles of record management.

1. Classification: All the records should be classified on the basis nature of records.The documents can be classified on the basis of appropriate method o classification.

2. Purpose: Record should be maintained with justifiable and clear purpose while maintaining the record, the purpose o record keeping should be dear. Recordw without purpose are a waste of time, labour & money.

3. Flexibility : The record management should be flexible. There must be the chances of expansion or contraction of document as per the requirement of the business.

4. Economy: While maintaining the record the cost factor should be considered. Therefore the valuable record should be recorded systematically and useless should be disposed timely.

5. Retention: The main objective records management is to preserve the required documents for future reference. Therefore, all the records should be maintained in such a way so that the required information can be obtained easily and quickly.

6. Verification: There must be evidence of all the document which are preserved in an office. The maintenance of records without any evidential proof will be worthless because they cannot fulfill the legal requirements.

Retention and disposal of Records

Retention of Records: Retention of records refers to preservation of documents for future reference. Records are the memory of business. They have specific purpose, they help in corporate decision making. They detect errors, frauds and irregularities. Thus, retention of records is very essential. All records don’t have equal value and importance. Vital or very important records should be kept at very safety place, important records should be kept at current file, useful records should be kept at store and non-essential or off-dated records should be disposed. Records retention schedule should be prepared by the organizations to make it systematic and scientific. The basic steps of records retention are as follows:

  1. Analyzing the cost of existing procedures to serve as basis for comparisons.
  2. Preparing a physical inventory of all type of records.
  3. Seeking opinions of all manager concerned.
  4. Seeking approval of the retention schedule from CEO.
  5. Communication of retention schedule to ensure its implementation.
  6. Review of retention schedule.

Disposal of records: Disposition refers to the final decision about whether to dispose of records or keep permanently. Actually disposal of record is a process of destroying useless, off-dated and unnecessary records or document. Records, which are not any longer required, should be disposed as per rules or schedule. If useless, off-dated and unnecessary records are kept for long period, the office would be warehouse a records, which increase space and labor cost and decrease efficiency in performance. Thus, disposal of records is very essential. Organization should lay down clear-cut policy regarding, disposal of records. There may be government rules and regulations on this matter.

According to document disposal Act. 2027;  record are classified into six categories on the basis of their usefulness and important. They are:

  1. Never disposal
  2. Disposable after 20 years
  3. Disposable after 10 years
  4. Disposable after 3 years
  5. Disposable after 1 years

Important Questions

  1. Explain the types of records [8]
  2. What do you mean by record management? Explain the importance of record management for an office. [2+6]
  3. What is records management? Explain the principle of record management. [8]
  4. Show the importance of retention and disposal of office records [8]
